title: Stalk description of the extension-by-zero base-change morphism
statement: Let $U'\xrightarrow{g_U}U$ and $X'\xrightarrow{g}X$ form a cartesian square [def-cbc-open-immersion-square] with open immersions $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ and $j':U'\hookrightarrow X'$. For an abelian sheaf $F$ on $U_{\mathrm{Et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero], let $\beta:g^{-1}j_!F\to j'_!g_U^{-1}F$ be the canonical base-change morphism, inverse to the mate, under $j'_!\dashv j'^{-1}$ [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction], of the composite $g_U^{-1}F\to g_U^{-1}j^{-1}j_!F\simeq j'^{-1}g^{-1}j_!F$. At every geometric point $\bar x'$ of $X'$, with $\bar x=g\bar x'$, the induced map on geometric stalks is the inverse-image stalk isomorphism $F_{\bar u}\simeq (g_U^{-1}F)_{\bar u'}$ when $\bar x'$ lies in $U'$ (where $\bar u'$ and $\bar u$ are the corresponding points), and is the unique map $0\to0$ when $\bar x'$ lies outside $U'.

source.place: Lemma 03S6 (base change for extension by zero), proof and adjunction construction

proof.text: Fix a geometric point \bar x' of X' and let \bar x=g\bar x'. By the extension-by-zero stalk formula, the stalk of g^{-1}j_!F at \bar x' identifies with F_{\bar u} when \bar x=j\bar u lies in U and is zero otherwise; the stalk of j'_!g_U^{-1}F identifies with (g_U^{-1}F)_{\bar u'} when \bar x'=j'\bar u' lies in U' and is zero otherwise. The inverse-image stalk identification identifies (g_U^{-1}F)_{\bar u'} with F_{\bar u} for corresponding geometric points.

source.place: Proposition 03S5 (proposition-describe-jshriek), explicit map on germ representatives; geometric-point inverse-image identification as in lem-kun-stalk-as-pullback

proof.text: Write $H=g^{-1}j_!F$, $K=g_U^{-1}F$, and $\alpha:K\to j'^{-1}H$ for the composite in the statement; let $\mu:j'_!K\to H$ be its adjoint, so that $\beta=\mu^{-1}$. The chosen cartesian identification gives $\bar x\in U$ if and only if $\bar x'\in U'$. Suppose first $\bar x'=j'\bar u'$ and $\bar x=j\bar u$. The unit $F\to j^{-1}j_!F$ is the adjoint of the identity of $j_!F$. The explicit adjunction formula therefore sends a section $s\in F(V)$, with $V$ an etale object over $U$, to its image in the sheafification of $j_{p!}F$ on that same object. The inside stalk formula sends this image back to the germ $[s]\in F_{\bar u}$. Thus the unit is the identity under the canonical inside-stalk identifications. Taking inverse image along $g_U$ and using $j'^{-1}g^{-1}=g_U^{-1}j^{-1}$ shows that $\alpha_{\bar u'}$ is the identity under the identifications of Step 1. The explicit adjunction formula for $j'$ sends the germ of a section of $K$ on a neighbourhood inside $U'$ to its image under $\alpha$; hence $\mu_{\bar x'}$ is the identity under those identifications. Its inverse $\beta_{\bar x'}$ is therefore precisely $F_{\bar u}\simeq K_{\bar u'}$. If $\bar x'$ is outside $U'$, cartesianness puts $\bar x$ outside $U$; Step 1 makes both stalks zero, and the stalk of $\beta$ is the unique map $0\to0$.
